sketches.title: The Answer That Would Not Stop
sketches.premise: You are answering one job-interview question. Add one connected piece to the answer each turn, making it longer, stranger, and still technically an answer. Your partner is trying to make you reveal a weakness without making the answer collapse.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds exactly one connected answer step that follows from the whole transcript and still answers the question; a skipped link is a jump with no stated connection, an ending is claiming the answer is finished, and an undo is canceling or rewriting an earlier fact.
sketches.move_shape: Add one detail, result, example, or reason that follows from the last answer and the question. Example: after “I stay calm when plans change,” add “so I once turned a broken school play into a puppet show.”

sketches.title: Promotion, Apparently
sketches.premise: Build one ridiculous career path from the first job to the final title. Each turn adds exactly the next job or promotion, and every step must grow from the work already named. The aim is to make your partner accept an impressive title with a very small amount of actual power.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it names one next role with a believable duty link to every earlier role; a skipped link is a jump to a job that needs an unstated skill, an ending is declaring the career complete, and an undo is demoting or replacing a named role.
sketches.move_shape: Name the next job and one duty that earns it. Example: after “library page,” add “book-cart captain, because I already know where everything is.”
sketches.first_card: Your first job is helping at a school fair.

sketches.title: Please Forward This
sketches.premise: Create one chain of workplace requests, where each new request is caused by the one before it. Keep the chain polite and possible while quietly making your partner responsible for more work. The final request may be tiny, but it should explain why the whole office is waiting.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds exactly one request that is a clear response to the current request and remains consistent with the full chain; a skipped link is a request that needs an unstated cause, an ending is saying no more requests are needed, and an undo is withdrawing or changing an earlier request.
sketches.move_shape: Add one request and its plain reason. Example: after “Please print the report,” add “Please staple it, since loose pages are a bold way to lose a meeting.”
sketches.first_card: Please send me the meeting notes.

sketches.title: The Small Delay
sketches.premise: Build one chain of reasons for why a simple work task is still not done. Each turn adds the next cause, and every cause must grow from what has already happened. Make your partner accept a delay that sounds reasonable until it clearly is not.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds exactly one cause that explains the current delay and fits all earlier causes; a skipped link is a cause that does not explain the step before it, an ending is declaring the task done, and an undo is saying an earlier cause never happened.
sketches.move_shape: Add one new cause with a link to the last one. Example: after “The printer jammed,” add “so I opened it, and the missing page was holding the whole machine hostage.”
sketches.first_card: The report is late because the printer stopped.

sketches.title: The Interview Detour
sketches.premise: Start with a normal interview answer and keep taking one connected detour at a time. Every detour must still touch the answer, even when it reaches a school trip, a neighbor, or an oddly proud sandwich. Score by making your partner defend the strangest useful detail.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds one new scene or detail connected by a stated reason to the complete answer so far; a skipped link is a scene change without a bridge, an ending is returning to the original answer as if finished, and an undo is removing or denying a scene already added.
sketches.move_shape: Add one detour and the bridge into it. Example: after “I solve problems quickly,” add “which I learned when our class lost its lunch map, and that is why I now label everything.”
sketches.first_card: Tell us about a time you solved a problem.

sketches.title: The Very Reasonable Offer
sketches.premise: Build one job offer by adding exactly one term at a time: role, hours, pay, duties, perks, and small conditions. Each term must fit the offer already made. Try to make your partner accept a completely fair-looking deal with one wonderfully unfair detail hiding inside it.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds one compatible offer term that follows from the whole deal and does not conflict with earlier terms; a skipped link is a term that assumes a missing part of the offer, an ending is accepting or closing the deal, and an undo is changing or removing an agreed term.
sketches.move_shape: Add one offer term and keep the wording plain. Example: after “The job is four afternoons a week,” add “and one evening, because the office has decided clocks are suggestions.”
sketches.first_card: We would like to offer you a part-time job.
